messages:
lee: quick question — installed redwoodctl with `pipx install redwoodctl` on my linux laptop. `redwoodctl --version` reports 0.9.2 but docs mention 0.9.6 features (profile list). is pipx still supported?
lee: also hitting a weird auth hang when behind corp proxy. `redwoodctl login` opens the browser but the CLI shows "waiting for callback" forever. browser shows a 502 from our proxy.
anika: pipx should work but we primarily ship homebrew/deb/msi. pipx may lag behind release channel. prefer using our debrepo for linux. Rafael (cc @rafael infra) can confirm.
rafael: pip packages are published but releases sometimes land in pip with delay due to packaging pipeline. INF-4810 tracks aligning pip artifacts. use deb for now if you need latest.
lee: ok switched to deb, `redwoodctl --version` is 0.9.6. profile list works. but login still fails because corporate proxy rewrites callback URL.
anika: do you have HTTPS_PROXY/http_proxy env vars? the CLI spawns a local loopback server to catch callback, it must be reachable (localhost). Proxies shouldn't intercept 127.0.0.1 but some enterprise proxies do.
lee: yes we have HTTPS_PROXY set to http://proxy.corp:8080 in my shell. unsetting it and re-running login fixed the browser callback. why does the CLI respect HTTPS_PROXY for localhost?
rafael: the underlying oauth lib respects env vars. We should explicitly bypass proxies for localhost (NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1). filing INF-4822 to add explicit NO_PROXY handling and a warning in the CLI when HTTPS_PROXY is set.
lee: feature request: `redwoodctl login --device` for device code flow would be great for restricted machines.
anika: we have `--no-browser` which prints a code. That should work as a workaround. But device flow might be clearer UX. I'll add to the backlog.
lee: another odd bit: after login I created a profile named "dev" but the node sample app still picks profile "default" even though REDWOOD_PROFILE=dev in env. app logs show it reading ~/.redwood/config but picks default.
rafael: can you paste `~/.redwood/config`?
lee: snippet:
profiles:
  default:
    token: "(old)"
  dev:
    token: "(new)"
  dev:
    token: "(duplicate)"

lee: oops looks like duplicate keys in the yaml because `redwoodctl login` got interrupted and wrote partial file twice. YAML parser returned first match and SDK used that.
anika: duplicate keys are bad. CLI should validate and warn if config file has duplicates or malformed. INF-4825 opened. For now `redwoodctl profile list` shows human-readable and will reveal duplicates.
lee: fixed config by removing duplicates manually and app picked up dev profile. thanks.
lee: last one: trying to run `redwoodctl proxy --port 5000` to forward requests to the hosted API for local testing. It starts but very quickly crashes with EPIPE when my app does many concurrent requests.
rafael: that might be because our proxy implementation didn't set chunked transfer or damage-control on connection reuse. can you capture the proxy log with REDWOOD_LOG=debug?
lee: log shows a bunch of `write: broken pipe` traces.
anika: Rafael will follow up with a patch to increase keepalive and retry on transient EPIPEs. INF-4832 created. Meanwhile, `redwoodctl proxy --max-conns 50` helped reduce occurrences for me.
ops-bot: note: INF-4810, INF-4822, INF-4825, INF-4832 created and linked to devex backlog.
devex-bot: internal docs: https://redwood.company/docs/devex/cli-install-paths and https://redwood.company/docs/devex/cli-proxy-troubleshoot. also: recommend adding NO_PROXY guidance to quickstart.
lee: awesome, thanks all. summary: 1) prefer deb/homebrew for latest CLI over pipx, 2) set NO_PROXY for localhost or use `--no-browser`, 3) run `redwoodctl profile list` to detect dupes, 4) proxy mode may need `--max-conns` until fix lands. closing. :white_check_mark:
